titulo.texto: Maximilian and Carlota in the Garden

frase_gancho.texto: In eighteen sixty-five, the emperors of Mexico chose this garden to spend the summer and to give concerts beside the pond.

puente_narrativo.texto: If you want a little extra, the last stop is optional: Cantinflas’s vacation house, on Benito Juárez Boulevard. It is not always open.

guion_corto.texto: In eighteen sixty-five, a European emperor chose this garden as his summer home. Maximilian of Habsburg and his wife, Carlota, picked it after returning from a trip to Yucatán. With them, the old Borda house became an Imperial Palace, and stopped working as a hotel. They held grand gatherings and concerts beside the pond. It was a brief episode: Maximilian ruled Mexico for little more than three years. The garden later welcomed other visitors, such as Francisco I. Madero, Emiliano Zapata and Porfirio Díaz. Today it is a cultural center with exhibitions, a bookstore and an open-air auditorium. It is a good place to think about how power and nature meet in a single landscape.

guion_largo.texto:
Maximilian of Habsburg was an Austrian archduke who came to Mexico in eighteen sixty-four to be emperor. His wife, Carlota, was the daughter of the king of Belgium. The two looked for a place to rest outside the capital, and they found it in Cuernavaca.

In eighteen sixty-five they chose this garden as their summer home, after their trip to Yucatán. The old Borda house, which until then had worked as a hotel, became an Imperial Palace. Another source states that between eighteen sixty-four and eighteen sixty-six the emperor used the Palace of Cortés as a summer residence. The sources do not agree on that detail, so this stop focuses on the garden.

Life in the garden with the emperors was full of celebrations. Grand gatherings and concerts were held over the pond. Imagine the lake with lights and musicians, and the court strolling along the terraces. It is a very European image for a Mexican garden, and that is part of its interest.

To understand why they chose this place, think about what Cuernavaca offered: mild weather, water, shade and flowers. These were reasons of rest, but also of taste. A European court was looking for a landscape where it could feel at home.

As you walk, try to locate the main house and the lake. Imagine the walks and the evening gatherings between one and the other. That is how you understand why a garden could also serve as a political stage.

There is one detail worth keeping in mind. Maximilian and Carlota arrived in a country in the middle of a dispute. Their stay in Cuernavaca was a rest within a political project that did not last. It is a pleasure garden born from a mining fortune that served a fleeting court.

The episode was short. Carlota traveled to Europe in eighteen sixty-six to ask for help and never returned to Mexico. Maximilian was executed by firing squad in Querétaro in eighteen sixty-seven. With his death, the empire came to an end.

The garden remained an important place. According to one source, it later welcomed Porfirio Díaz, Francisco I. Madero and Emiliano Zapata. It is a list that crosses very different projects for the country: the empire, the Porfiriato, the Revolution. One single garden saw them all.

Today it is called the Jardín Borda Cultural Center. It has exhibition halls, a bookstore and an open-air auditorium, where painting, sculpture, photography, dance, theater and concerts are presented. It is classified as a historic monument.

The question this stop leaves us with is simple. Why do the powerful always choose the same places? Mild weather, water, shade and flowers explain quite a bit. But as you walk here, you can also think about who made that beauty possible. The gardeners, the bricklayers and the workers of the mine that paid for everything do not appear in the chronicles, but they were there.

texto.pregunta: Myth: Maximilian lived in Cuernavaca until his death.
texto.respuesta: Reality: He used the garden as a summer home. He was executed by firing squad in Querétaro in eighteen sixty-seven.
